About

Analytics with business judgment built in.

I'm a business-oriented Data Analyst trained through the Digital Egypt Pioneers Initiative in Python, SQL, Power BI and Excel — but my background isn't limited to a classroom.

Before and during that training, I spent two years inside Telecom Egypt (WE), first in Sales and now supporting the Audit team, reviewing operational data across branches for compliance. That combination means I approach a dataset the way someone who has actually worked inside a business does: looking for what it means operationally, not just what it looks like on a chart.

My work is grounded in careful data cleaning and exploratory analysis, clear visualization, and — most importantly — explaining findings in a way non-technical stakeholders can act on.

Project 01

Sales Performance Dashboard

Nexora Retail Group · fictional company portfolio project
Power BI Power Query DAX Star Schema Data Visualization

An end-to-end Power BI solution built to evaluate retail sales performance, customer segments and regional drivers. U.S. retail transactions were cleaned and validated in Power Query, modeled as a star schema, analyzed with DAX measures and presented in an interactive executive dashboard.

Dataset

9,800 transaction rows · 18 columns

Time horizon

2015–2018, four years of sales data

Data preparation

Corrected data types, isolated 11 missing Postal Code entries, engineered Shipping Days and Product Keys

Key Insights

  1. $2.26M in total sales from 4,922 orders across 793 customers, with an average order value of $459.48.
  2. Technology is the highest-performing category, followed by Furniture and Office Supplies.
  3. Consumer is the largest customer segment by order count and revenue. Corporate contributes significant commercial volume with strong average order values.
  4. West is the top-performing region, followed by East, Central and South.
  5. Technology × West is the strongest category–region pairing, with Technology × East as the secondary leader.
  6. Sales cluster toward the end of each calendar year, with stable monthly patterns and no unexpected anomalies across 2015–2018.
  7. Shipping took 0 to 7 days, averaging 3.96 days across all recorded transactions.

Project 02

Population & Camp Analytics

Population and camp records by country, city and site · 2017–2018
Python Pandas / NumPy Matplotlib / Seaborn Excel PivotTables & Slicers

An exploratory analysis and interactive dashboard built on population and accommodation records from four countries. Python was used to load, audit and explore the dataset, while Excel PivotTables and slicers power an executive dashboard filterable by year, country, city and site.

Dataset

9,917 records · 12 columns

Time horizon

January 2017 to November 2018

Countries

Iraq, Libya, Syria and Yemen

Key Insights

  1. 59.01M total members across four countries. Yemen holds the largest share at 40.61% (23.96M), followed by Syria at 32.97% (19.46M).
  2. Female members make up 56.70% of the population (33.45M) versus 43.30% male (25.55M).
  3. Population declined 4.24% from 30.14M in 2017 to 28.86M in 2018.
  4. 1.19M accommodation units in total. Flats are the largest type (456,167) and houses the smallest (181,725).
  5. Missing values are confined to four columns: Room, Flat, House and Tent. Every other column is fully populated.
  6. Members correlate strongly with female (0.91) and male (0.87) counts. Room, Flat and House move together perfectly (1.00), while Tent is strongly negatively correlated with all three (−0.90).
  7. Houses have a modest positive relationship with members (0.30). The scatter plot with a regression line shows a positive linear trend and a wide spread across countries.
